newsitem.title: USA: Alberto-Culver sees earnings tempered by investing.
newsitem.headline: Alberto-Culver sees earnings tempered by investing.

text.p: Alberto-Culver Co said Thursday it continues to invest heavily in competitive markets and this may may temper earnings growth in the second half of its fiscal year.
But the personal care products company said it still expects to report record 1997 sales and earnings.

"In very competitive markets, we continue to invest heavily to support our businesses and, while that may somewhat temper our rate of earnings growth in the second half, we remain on track for another record sales and earnings year," President and Chief Executive Howard Bernick said.
Alberto-Culver posted fiscal second quarter earnings of $0.31 per primary share versus $0.25 a year earlier.

Alberto-Culver USA posted a 20 percent increase in sales and a 50 percent rise in profits, boosted by St. Ives Laboratories, which it acquired last year. The unit's core domestic brands and shipments of new products showed positive growth trends, it said.
The company said its Sally Beauty Co ended the quarter with 1,765 stores and posted double-digit profit and sales increases.
Alberto-Culver International was pressured by the strength of the dollar, especially in the Scandanavian countries, but the unit still posted a double-digit profit rise, the parent company said.
